situation: Small German family foundry for which we are a big customer: 7.1 % of turnover, and our weight rises once it loses about a fifth of its turnover from January 2027 (news:20261015-S14). Its bank is watching its liquidity closely. It has asked us to pay within 10 days from November and to confirm firm Q1 call-offs (doc:20261019-70190-S13), so the 'stable' financial signal is now questionable. Power is bought forward and material covered to Dec 2028, so it still offers a price fixed until then; market-energy arguments are 'not our reality'. The casing cover is priced at should-cost (33.94 vs 33.93), while the HB 40 housing (43.39) carries margin and is 35 % above Tarsevi. It is the qualified backup for three distressed suppliers' parts (310011, 310020, 310030), on our tooling, so its own liquidity strain concentrates risk.

update_notes.summary: Pfaffenreuth loses about a fifth of its turnover from January after a heating customer moved its castings to Eastern Europe. Its bank is watching liquidity, and it asks us for 10-day payment from November plus firm Q1 call-offs. This gives us payment-term and volume levers to trade for price, especially on the margin-carrying HB 40 housing (310060). It is also a new supply risk, because Pfaffenreuth is our backup for three distressed suppliers' parts.
